independent.summary: `const signupEmail = email.trim()` sits OUTSIDE the try/catch, so a non-string `email` (e.g. `{"email": 42}` or `["a@b.c"]` — the required-field check only tests truthiness) throws TypeError inside an async Express 4 handler; there is no global `unhandledRejection` handler in backend/index.js, so an unauthenticated POST /auth/onboard kills the whole backend process. On main the same `email.trim()` lived inside the try and merely returned 500, and this diff defensively wrote `String(alphaCode).trim()` while leaving email unguarded — a regression in handling of untrusted input.

The domain claim is still check-then-act: `claimCheck` reads `Entity.exists`/`User.exists`, then ~250ms of bcrypt(12) and `User.create` run before the Entity upsert. Two concurrent signups naming the same unclaimed domain both pass the check; the loser's upsert hits the unique index on `Entity.domain` (E11000) → 500, but its `User` with `roles: ['owner']` for that domain was already created and is never deleted, leaving a second, loginable owner on the winner's entity (conversations, settings, billing). The new comment "Nothing has been created yet… the upsert only ever inserts" is false under concurrency, while the alpha-code consume in the same block was made atomic precisely for this class of race.

The catch-all `releaseAlphaCode` refunds the code use for failures that happen AFTER the User and Entity were created (e.g. a throw in `user.save()` or the token push): the `$inc: -1`/`$pull` returns the slot while a loginable owner account and its Entity persist, so a `maxUses: 1` alpha code can be spent a second time even though the first signup did claim a domain. No compensating cleanup of the created User/Entity exists.

The item's promise that a stranger cannot claim a domain someone else owns is not achieved: `POST /auth/register`, public and unauthenticated in the same file and mounted at backend/index.js:40, takes `entityDomain` and `role` straight from the body and writes `memberships: [{ entityDomain, roles: [role || 'owner'] }]` with no alpha code, no claim check and no role whitelist — so the LEO-108 guard on /onboard is bypassable (and `role: 'superadmin'` is self-assignable). Pre-existing rather than introduced here, but it leaves the fixed boundary wide open.

The claim check compares only the newly normalized form, so any Entity or membership stored un-normalized by another path (`/auth/register`, a scrape upsert, superadmin creation — none of which call `normalizeDomain`, e.g. `www.example.com` or mixed case) is invisible to `Entity.exists({ domain: claimDomain })`; a signup for that site passes the guard and gets a second entity for the same domain, which the widget's `window.location.hostname` fallback can then route visitor traffic to. No normalization of existing records or of the other write paths accompanies the new rule.

triageGrades.reason: The change rewrites the signup/auth route POST /auth/onboard, its credential (alpha-code) consumption and its authorization-granting membership write.
No credentials, keys or tokens are introduced or handled differently; only an optional log-level env var is documented.
Billing/Stripe code is untouched (billing is only mentioned in prose about what an owner can see).
Right call even with weak line evidence: the new `releaseAlphaCode` does `$inc: { useCount: -1 }` plus a `$pull` that deletes a `usedBy` entry, and the Entity `$set`/upsert write path is altered.
No outbound HTTP/SDK calls are added or changed; the notifications service only appears as a stub inside the new test.
No CI, deploy, nixpacks/railway or migration files change; the one `.env.example` addition is an optional var with a safe in-code default.

summary: The local review reported nothing at all and so missed a crash-level unvalidated-input regression plus the residual claim race and the public /auth/register bypass that undercuts the fix; its triage calls, however, were all defensible.
